The local observatory records seasonal changes in the rivers and gardens surrounding the town. Volunteers compare careful measurements every morning, and the resulting records help researchers understand how the environment responds to changing weather.

During the summer the team installed a second weather station near the old bridge. Its readings confirm the observations from the first station, while a separate notebook records the plants and animals found nearby. These independent sources make the conclusions more reliable.

The researchers plan to publish their methods together with the measurements. Other towns will be able to repeat the experiment and compare results across different landscapes, helping the community decide which restoration projects should receive attention next year.
